preamble: Stopping of the alveolar fricative [s] to [t] in syllable codas, where a final sibilant surfaces as unreleased [t̚]. Thai, which allows only stops and sonorants in the coda, pronounces final s in Indic and English loanwords as [t̚] (Pali rasa > รส rót, English gas > แก๊ส kɛ́ːt), and Middle Korean coda s merged with t in modern Korean (wós > 옷 [ot̚]). In Chatino (Zapotecan) the change was unconditioned: Proto-Chatino *s became t throughout Core Chatino (*sejeʔ 'salt' > Tataltepec tejeꞌ), while Teojomulco kept s.

examples.note: A final sibilant surfaces as unreleased [t̚]; the Lao cognate is ລົດ.
The coda s of the English loanword is pronounced [t̚]; a spelling pronunciation /kɛːs˦˥/ also exists.
Coda s merged with t; [s] returns before a vowel-initial suffix, as in 옷이 [osi].
Same coda neutralization of s to unreleased [t̚].
